text: Every screen and button in Scout checks what the person is allowed to do. Here's where that comes from, so you can set it up right the first time.
The one thing to remember: what a person can do is their roles, plus anything granted to them individually. Nothing else gives access.
Access is set in Settings.
Open the Staff menu,
and choose Staff.
Let's look at a technician, Tess Holt.
Open the Access tab. It shows everything about what she can do.
First, her roles. She has one: Technician.
Below are the things that role lets her do, grouped by area.
Hover over any line to see where it comes from. This one comes from her Technician role.
Individual permissions add one thing for one person, like covering for a manager on leave.
They only add. To take something away, change the role.
The license is separate.
Signing a SOAP needs a veterinary license. No role or grant replaces it.
Roles themselves are set up in the Staff menu,
under Roles.
Each role is either per office, like Technician,
or practice-wide, like Client Liaison.
An office role decides which office's stock and automatic tasks a person gets. That's why the office matters.
Two more rules. Nobody can change their own access. And every change is logged, with who made it.
The most common mistake is making someone an admin to fix one missing button. Give the right role, or grant that one permission.
Remember: what a person can do is their roles plus their individual grants. Nothing else gives access.
